summary: Naresh Keerthi works in Indology and linguistics. He was at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from 2018 to 2021 and became an assistant professor at Ashoka University in 2021.

Nariaki Nakazato is an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Toyo Bunko, Kobe University, and served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1997–2010).
Narimoto Tamayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1974 and 1988.

Nashalla Gwyn Nyinda works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Naropa University, Chagpori Tibetan Medical Institute, Shang Shung Institute, Qinghai University, and ITEA, she became clinic director at Nyinda Clinic in 2009 and president of Chagpori in 2022.

Natalie Depraz is a philosopher educated at ENS de Fontenay-Saint-Cloud and Paris Nanterre University. She founded the Rouen School of Phenomenology and held professorships at the University of Rouen Normandy and Paris Nanterre University.
Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She was affiliated with Harvard University (attested 2001) and was appointed professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Stephan V. Beyer and also studied under Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.

Natalie Quli is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt and the Graduate Theological Union, and holds the Yehan Numata Professorship of Buddhist Studies at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Natalie Rothman is a historian. She completed her studies at the University of Michigan (1999–2006) and took up a post at the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natalya Julianovna Lubotskaya was an Indologist who studied at Moscow State Pedagogical University (~1950–1955). She served as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences from 1957 to 1976.

Natalya Mikhailovna Sazanova was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied history at Moscow State University (~1949–1954). She taught at Moscow State University starting in 1958 and became a professor there in 1989.

Natalya Vasilyevna Dyakonova was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, historical, and Buddhist studies who studied at Saint Petersburg State University. She held posts at the Ukrainian Oriental Institute, the Institute of Oriental Studies, and the State Hermitage Museum.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2005. She held appointments at UC Berkeley, UCLA, and became an associate professor at the University of Virginia in 2017.

Natasha Reichle is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Joanna Gottfried Williams, also studying under Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, and others.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who earned her PhD under Hans T. Bakker at the University of Groningen, where she also held a post between 2010 and 2018.
Nathan Brown was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Japanology. He studied at Williams College and Newton Theological Institution, and founded the American Baptist Missionary Union in 1837.
Nathan Sivin was a Sinologist and historian educated at MIT and Harvard. He taught at MIT from 1966 to 1977 and served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania from 1977 to 2006.

Nathan Söderblom was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Uppsala University, the Sorbonne, and EPHE, he held professorships of history of religion at Uppsala University (1901–1912) and the University of Leipzig (1912–1914).

Nathan W. Hill is a linguist, Tibetologist, and Sinologist who studied under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff, and at Harvard. He served as principal investigator at SOAS (~2008–2019) and at Trinity College Dublin from 2019.

Nathaniel Brassey Halhed was an Indologist and linguist educated at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford. He served as an official for the East India Company (~1771–1785) and later as secretary at East India House (1809).
